5._section_summary: This Measures section describes daily-diary adaptations of several instruments used in the present study, including newly developed items assessing frequency of interactions with body-focused others, the Self-Compassion Scale–Short Form (SCS-SF), the Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2), the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), body image concern items from the EDE-Q, and the negative affect items from the PANAS. The section reports internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) across study days for each measure and notes that PCA identified a body-focused-others factor used in analyses.

6.evidence_source: Four multilevel models were run in SAS 9.3 with raw scores on intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, and negative affect across study days serving as the criteria variables.
6._section_summary: This section describes the analytic strategy for a single daily-diary study using multilevel modeling to separate within-person (daily) and between-person (weekly) variance; predictors were disaggregated into person means and daily deviations and centered. Four multilevel models were run (for intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, and negative affect) with BMI as a covariate, and interactions between daily/weekly self-compassion and daily/weekly frequency of interactions with body-focused others were tested and probed with simple slopes.

It summarizes within-person and between-person correlations, noting that BMI (assessed once) was negatively associated with body appreciation at the between-persons level, and that higher self-compassion related to greater intuitive eating and body appreciation and lower negative affect. The text does not label any study as 'Study 1' or report sample size, participant demographics, measurement instruments (e.g., BAS/BAS-2), or numeric correlation coefficients.

12._section_summary: This section reports central multilevel analyses examining interactions between self-compassion and frequency of interactions with body-focused others on outcomes (intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, negative affect). It summarizes significant within-person (daily) and between-person (weekly) interactions: higher daily frequency of body-focused interactions predicted poorer outcomes on low-self-compassion days but reversed or attenuated on high-self-compassion days; at the between-person level, higher mean frequency predicted lower intuitive eating and body appreciation for low/average self-compassion but not for high self-compassion. The section does not label multiple studies (no 'Study 1' etc.).

14._section_summary: This section outlines the contributions and implications of the present study, emphasizing that state-level increases in self-compassion (within-person) benefit young adult women's affect, body image, and eating when facing body-image threats. It contrasts these within-person findings with prior between-person research and highlights practical implications for applying self-compassion strategies on a given day.

15.evidence_source: There were several limitations to the present study.
15._section_summary: This section outlines limitations of the present (single) study, noting its correlational, self-report, and measurement constraints and the inability to infer temporal or causal relationships. It also suggests future research directions such as experimental manipulation of self-compassion, more fine-grained (within-day) assessment, and use of longer or more objective measures to disentangle perceptions of others from their actual behaviors.
